# dsh-openrouter-plus

**Service-tier routing *and* a live model list for OpenRouter — as a DeepSeek Harness plugin, with
n
o patched packages.**
DSH's OpenRouter support has two gaps, and neither one is reachable from a provider profile.

**Routing.** OpenRouter lets you steer where a request is served from: `flex` endpoints bill half
pr

ice on a slower pool, `priority` endpoints bill a multiplier for lower latency, and the throughput
o
r price comparators reorder the pool in between. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` exposes `baseURL` and

`headers` on a provider profile, but no request-body fields
(discussion #9787).

**Model discovery.** *Fetch available models* is answered from the catalog baked into
`@earendil-wor

ks/pi-ai`, and for a catalog-backed route (`openrouter`) it answers **before** it reads
that route's

`baseURL`. The snapshot only refreshes when pi-ai is published again, so every model
OpenRouter has

added since then is invisible — on the build this plugin was written against, that was
**65 of Open

Router's 463 live models**, including `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`,
`moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro` and `x-ai/g

rok-4.20-multi-agent`. Pointing the row at another endpoint
does not help: the provider *name* is wh
at short-circuits, not the URL.
This plugin closes both gaps from the outside, and it never patches a shipped package. A **loopback
relay** applies the routing preset to each request. **Sync live models** reads the endpoint a route
points at and lists it, so you can tick the models you want and add just those. Both ride on schema

fields the profile already has, so both survive `bun install -g` upgrades and never touch
`~/.bun/in

file already has, so both survive `bun install -g` upgrades and never touch
`~/.bun/install/global`.
The preset is chosen **per session, at request time**. One provider row keeps serving every preset,

## What you get

- **Sync live models.** A provider row routed through OpenRouter Plus also gets a **Sync live
models

…** button. It reads the endpoint that row points at and shows what it publishes *right
now* — inclu

ding models added after the pi-ai catalog in your install was generated — with a
filter box and a ch

eckbox per model. Tick what you want and only those are added; models the
route already declares are

marked `added` and cannot be added twice. Nothing is rewritten:
hand-written names, context windows

and effort maps are left exactly as they are. A row that is
not routed shows the switch alone: the

button belongs to the opt-in, not to every `llm-pi-ai` card.
- **One provider row, any preset.** A r

outed provider keeps its key, protocol and models and gains
one thing: a composable **preset** that

the relay applies to each request. No per-preset provider
copies, no sibling route per preset, no mo

del list duplicated nine times.
- **Pin one endpoint, not just a tier.** A fourth thing the chip can

set: a specific upstream
endpoint (`relace/fp4`, `deepinfra/fp8/priority`) read from the model's li

ve listing. A pin is a
*hard* pin — `provider.only` plus `allow_fallbacks: false` — so a request goe

s to that endpoint or
surfaces the upstream error, instead of quietly landing somewhere else. Pickin

g one **disables**
the Tier and Precision cells and shows the endpoint's own values, because the end

point already
decided both.
- **Speed beside the price.** Each endpoint row in that menu can also st

ate how fast it is — output
tokens per second and milliseconds to the first token, OpenRouter's own

rolling 30-minute
percentiles — read with your key on the first request that names the model, and re

freshed as you
use it. Five facts do not fit one 220 px row, so Settings → OpenRouter Plus carries a

checkbox per
fact and a choice between the median and the median-plus-p90.
- **Pinned base URLs** f

or what a chip cannot cover — `/v1` (no pin), `/default/v1` (Standard),
`/flex/v1` (Flex), `/priorit

y/v1` (Priority), `/ultrafast/v1` (Ultra). Paste one into an

## Spend: what it actually cost
The relay reports the **billed amount**, not a token count multiplied by a price list. Each response
carries `usage.cost` (plus `cost_details` for BYOK's upstream charge and server tools), and the rel

ay
copies it out of a bounded head/tail while forwarding the bytes untouched.

When the response does not describe itself, the relay asks OpenRouter. A Responses-API body
[该节后续省略]
## Security model

- **Loopback only.** The relay forwards the caller's `Authorization` verbatim and stores no key.
Do

not bind a routable interface.
- **The key is spent, never kept.** Two reads use the caller's own `A

uthorization` and nothing is
written after them: the generation lookup (when a response omits its pr

ovider or its bill) and one
endpoint-listing read per model per cache window, which is what puts lat

ency and throughput in the
provider menu. The **listing** read is refused when the request went to a

nother upstream, so a key
belonging to one provider is not presented to another. The generation look

up is older and always
asks this plugin's configured `upstream`, whichever mount the request arrived

on: a key belonging
to a third-party gateway is presented to OpenRouter only if that gateway answer

ed with a
generation id (`gen-…` or `X-Generation-Id`).
- **The control API rides the GUI's origin a

nd fence.** It is mounted on the DSH web server, so it
is reachable exactly where the GUI is and now

here else, and every browser request passes the same
Host/Origin check and session cookie the GUI's

own API uses. Only a loopback request with no
`Origin` — a local process — is exempt, and that is th

e privilege it already had on the relay
listener.
- **Read-only telemetry.** The status API exposes

counts, token sums and billed cost, never prompts
or keys.
- **Reversible by construction.** The plu

gin only ever adds a provider route whose `baseURL` points
at its own origin, and only removes route

s that pass that same test. The switch is the same idea
one level down: the endpoint it took over is

recorded in the plugin's config, and **Detach** —
or deleting the target — puts it back, so a provi
der is never left pointing at a dead mount.
